problems.title: The historical recipe placed entropy_top_ratio outside the actor configuration
problems.source_location: Eq. (2); current actor recipe, actor configuration declaration and dp_actor.py lines 440–461.
claim: Eq. (2) selects response tokens using ratio \(\rho=0.2\). The historical recipe supplies that setting through actor_rollout_ref.model.entropy_top_ratio, but verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py, lines 785–789, constructs the actor from the separate actor configuration branch. In verl/workers/actor/dp_actor.py, line 440, the actor looks up entropy_top_ratio in its own configuration and bypasses the helper when the setting is absent.
analysis: The historical recipe places entropy_top_ratio equal to \(0.2\) in the model branch, but the worker constructs its actor from the actor branch and the actor looks up the key there. That lookup yields None and bypasses high-entropy selection in favor of the full-response mask. The authors' subsequent fix moves both the setting and its structured declaration into the actor configuration.

At the current head, the recipe explicitly sets actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_top_ratio to \(0.2\), the actor dataclass/YAML declares the field, and the worker passes the actor branch. The historical missing-key lookup no longer applies.
result: The known configuration-delivery concern is already corrected in the current release. The author statement that published runs were unaffected is recorded as attribution, without independent recovery of their experiment provenance.
problems.impact_rationale: The latest recipe, declaration and lookup agree, clearing this historical release concern.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors moved and declared the setting consistently in the actor branch. This is a documented historical correction, not a newly validated full training run.

problems.title: An integer response mask was interpreted as index positions
claim: Historical verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py, get_global_entropy_top_mask, lines 53–87, flattens the response mask and uses it directly to index the flattened entropy tensor. The declared mask marks eligible response tokens, but an integer-valued mask has integer-index rather than Boolean-mask semantics. The author correction explicitly converts it to Boolean first.
analysis: For entropy values \((0.9,0.1)\) and an integer mask \((1,0)\), integer indexing gathers positions one and zero, yielding \((0.1,0.9)\), rather than the eligible singleton \((0.9)\). Subsequent selection can therefore map to the wrong token. The existing Boolean conversion changes the operation to eligibility filtering, as required.

Current line 68 explicitly converts the flattened mask to Boolean. For the same witness it filters the eligible singleton \((0.9)\) and maps its selected index back to the first position, yielding \((1,0)\). No integer-index ambiguity remains.
result: The current Boolean conversion removes the historical indexing witness. This does not certify arbitrary rounding boundaries, distributed execution or complete training.
problems.impact_rationale: The latest Boolean eligibility conversion clears the exhibited indexing error; full training remains outside this check.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors' existing correction converts response-mask eligibility to Boolean before filtering and mapping indices. No historical benchmark effect is quantified.

impact_rationale: The current recipe supplies the actor field and the helper converts integer masks to Boolean; both precise historical counterexamples are removed.
